_cite: Main!/Engn(s)!/Miss!/Wt! = Brandt-F16-A.xls tabs; TO = T.O. 1F-16A-1; Raymer = Raymer 6th ed.; Mattingly = Mattingly: Aircraft Engine Design, 2nd edition; todo = VnV/BrandtF16A/todo.md.
_aircraft_category_src: ONE canonical class flag for every discipline. Selects Raymer Tbl 12.3 (Cfe) / Raymer Tbl 15.2 + AE481 fractions (L2 weights) / Raymer 15.3.1 Fighter-Attack build-up (L3 weights) rows. Source tables name their categories differently, so each lookup translates this canonical value to its own row name -- see AeroL1.to_CLmax_table_row. Do NOT rename a table row to match this key.

geometry._src: Surface geometry = Brandt Main tab, column B (wing) / C (horizontal_tail) / H (vertical_tail), rows 18 = S_ft2, 19 = AR, 20 = taper, 21 = sweep_LE_deg, 22 = NACA 4-digit (last 2 digits = t/c %; wing B22 = 1404 -> 4%, corroborated TO Fig. 1-2 NACA 64A204). tc_root, tc_tip [TO Sec. I biconvex]. fuselage length_ft, max_width_ft, max_height_ft [Main!B32/C32/D32]. engine duct_length_ft [Main!F32, label E32 'Compr Face'].
geometry._note: Row map also in F16GeomL2.md / F16GeomL3.md §2. Derived quantities are Dependent getters; engine SLS thrust arrives by DI from .propulsion.T_SL.
geometry._overall_length_ft_src: L_aircraft, ft; feeds only the Raymer Eq. 12.44 (Amax/l)^2 term. Published F-16A length 47 ft 7.75 in = 47.6458 ft. Distinct from fuselage.length_ft.
geometry._TODO_overall_length_ft: overall_length_ft = 47.65 is traceable to no document in this repo; remove this key when pinned to a primary source. todo 2026-07-25 Phase 2 §6; Geom!B21 does not pin it (F16GeomL3.md §2).

aerodynamics._src: e_method 'official' [Raymer Eq. 12.48/12.49]; airfoil name [TO Fig. 1-2]; airfoiltype, design_CL [NACA 64A204 section data]; alpha_L0_deg, cl_max_2D, cl_alpha_per_deg [unpinned, see _TODO keys]; wave_drag_factor_E_WD [Brandt F-16A.xls Aero tab Sears-Haack wave-drag term, same source/value as f16a_L3.json]. Cfe is NOT an input: it is the aircraft_category-selected Raymer Tbl 12.3 row (AeroL2.lookup_Cfe), a published table constant rather than a design variable.

airfoil.name: NACA 64A204
airfoil._cite_alpha_L0_deg: -1.33 deg, from a compiled NACA 64A204 airfoil data summary (web-sourced 2026-07-30, corroborated by two independent searches). Caveat carried forward honestly: true 64A201-64A204 wind-tunnel data is scarce in the public literature; secondary sources (including this one) commonly estimate the 64A20X family from NACA 64A210 data. Not a primary NACA report. Was previously an unpinned -1.01 guarded by testTODO_AlphaL0Unverified (2026-07-25 Phase 3); replaced 2026-07-30.
airfoil._TODO_cl_max_2D: cl_max_2D = 1.20 (Abbott & von Doenhoff) conflicts with NTRS-19870017427's 1.0; remove when reconciled. Guard: TestAeroL2.testTODO_ClMax2DUnverified.
airfoil._TODO_cl_alpha_per_deg: cl_alpha = 0.105/deg is an internet-band midpoint, not primary-sourced; remove when pinned. Guard: TestAeroL2.testTODO_ClAlpha2DUnverified.

aerodynamics._TODO_wave_drag_factor_E_WD: E_WD = 2.2 is a tuned wave-drag multiplier back-checked to Brandt/Casey, not a measured F-16 datum; remove this key when sourced or accepted as a calibration knob. Same value/status as f16a_L3.json's identical key. Guard: TestAeroL2.testTODO_EWDCalibrationInput.
aerodynamics._amax_via_DI: Amax and L_aircraft are NOT aero inputs: both arrive by DI from the injected L2 geometry object (Amax a Dependent, FUSELAGE-ENVELOPE ellipse at L2, distinct from L3's area-ruled buildup; L_aircraft = .geometry.overall_length_ft).

propulsion._src: engine_type [F100-PW-200 class; selects the PropL2 Mattingly Eq. 3.55a/b TSFC coefficients]; engine_model [descriptor]; T_SL AB SLS lbf [Engn(s)!T_AB_SLS = Main!D29; TO Sec. I]; T_SL_mil, dry SLS lbf [Engn(s)!T_mil_SLS = Main!C29]; T_t4_max_F [Mattingly Tbl C.4, F100-PW-100]; TSFC_install_factor [Miss!C25 = Main!C25]; bypass_ratio [F100-PW-200 class; pinned to Nicolai & Carichner Table 14.3 F100-PW-100 -- see _cite_bypass_ratio key]
propulsion._note: Installed = uninstalled x 1.08. Brandt's stored SLS TSFCs (0.70 mil / 2.20 AB) are ALREADY installed -- do not double-apply [todo 2026-07-24 §4]. TR [Mattingly Eq. D.6] and T_SL_wet (= T_SL) are derived.
propulsion._cite_bypass_ratio: Nicolai & Carichner Table 14.3, F100-PW-100 (direct predecessor of the F100-PW-200 this model otherwise uses); temp_AI/docs/disciplines/reference_extracts/14_propulsion_fundamentals.md:581. Pinned 2026-07-30; was previously an unresolved _TODO_bypass_ratio marker (todo 2026-07-25 Phase 3).

weights._src: N_en [TO]; W_payload_fixed [Wt tab: crew + fixed equipment]; W_payload_expendable [Wt tab: stores]. Raymer Tbl 15.2 psf densities and the AE481 metabook §7 fractions are aircraft_category-selected toolbox Constants. S_strake_ft2/k_strake_psf [Brandt F-16A.xls Main!D18 / Wt!H7 -- Raymer Tbl 15.2 has NO strake/LERX category, so Brandt's own genuine INPUT assumption for this one component is the only available source; see F16WeightsL2.m's W_strake getter for the cross-model-borrow rationale].
weights._note: Exposed and fuselage wetted areas are injected live from F16GeomL2, not stored here. LG fraction 0.033 vs Brandt 0.034: todo 2026-07-24 §3c item 2. design_mach (Raymer Eq. 10.10 M^0.25) is NOT here either -- it is a REQUIREMENT, read from examples/F16A/f16a_requirements.json. NOT inputs: W_en (engine weight is computed from Raymer Eq. 10.10 using the injected prop object's T_SL and bypass_ratio, then x1.3 installed -- the x1.3 applies at L2 ONLY, F16WeightsL2.md §4) and W_energy (internal fuel is a mission-analysis output; Brandt Wt!B6 is back-calculated as W_TO - payload - OEW).
weights._strake_src: S_strake_ft2 = strake planform reference area [Brandt Main!D18 = 20 ft^2]; k_strake_psf = strake structural surface density [Brandt Wt!H7 = 4.5 lbf/ft^2]. W_strake = k_strake_psf * S_strake_ft2 = 90.00 lbf (added 2026-07-29 -- was previously an unmodeled ~13.7%-of-OEW gap, see examples/F16A/mds/weights_brandt_comparison.md section 5).

subsystems._note: NOT YET IMPLEMENTED -- no F16SubsystemsL2/F16LandingGearL2 class exists yet (docs/subplans/09_subsystems.md, Casey-approved, scribe-complete 2026-07-31; io pass 2026-07-31). Geometry-derived inputs: Raymer Eq. 7.14 fuselage volume off GeomL2's envelope-ellipse A_top/A_side, Roskam Eq. 6.2/6.3 wing volume, Nicolai Ch. 8 packaging/density tables, Raymer Ch. 11 landing-gear statistics. Universal textbook-equation coefficients (Raymer Eq. 7.14's 3.4 factor; Roskam Eq. 6.2's 0.54 coefficient and its own tau_w=(t/c)_tip/(t/c)_root definition, Eq. 6.3) are NOT duplicated here -- they belong in the future SubsystemsL2 toolbox code as equation constants, same code/JSON split already used for Raymer Eq. 12.48-12.51's coefficients in AeroL2. Full citation detail: docs/subplans/09_subsystems.md Equations & Citations §5-9c.

fuel._cite_fuel: Same selection/citation as f16a_L1.json .subsystems.fuel -- [Nicolai & Carichner, Table 8.6, p.210]; DECIDED (Casey, 2026-08-03): JP-8, not JP-4, per T.O. 1F-16A-1's own stated nominal internal-fuel type; see f16a_L1.json's _cite_fuel for the full note.
fuel._cite_packaging_factor: [Nicolai & Carichner, p.210, unnumbered 'Fuel Tank Packaging Factors' table] (docs/subplans/09_subsystems.md Equations & Citations §1) -- 'Integral tank — shallow fuselage' row = 0.80. CORRECTED (2026-08-03, re-scanned all 31 temp_AI reference-extract files including the newly-completed Nicolai Ch. 12/18-24 scrape per Casey's request -- no source anywhere states the F-16's actual tank construction type, so which of the table's five rows applies remains a judgment call, same as before). What changed: the io agent's original pick was 'Integral tank -- wing' (0.75), but this factor multiplies the FUSELAGE raw volume (Raymer Eq. 7.14 output) per subplan Eq. §5b, not the wing volume -- a fuselage-category row is the correct match regardless of which fuselage row (shallow vs deep) is picked. 'Shallow fuselage' (0.80) was chosen over 'deep fuselage' (0.85) as more representative of a slender fighter fuselage (F-16 max height 5.0 ft vs. length 46.5 ft) than a bomber/transport's deeper cross-section, but Nicolai gives no numerical shallow/deep threshold -- EXPLICIT JUDGMENT CALL, flag if 'deep fuselage' (0.85) is preferred instead. The full table belongs in the future SubsystemsL2 toolbox code as a Constant (same split as AeroL1.CLmax_table); this key only records which row is selected. Roskam's wing-volume formula (Eq. 6.2/6.3) already yields a usable volume and is NOT multiplied by a second packaging factor.

avionics._cite_density_lb_per_ft3: [Nicolai & Carichner, §8.1.11, p.210] flat average avionics density, 45 lb/ft3. DECIDED fidelity split (Casey, 2026-07-31; docs/subplans/09_subsystems.md Equations & Citations §4): L2/L3 switch from L1's Raymer-derived 37.5 lb/ft3 to Nicolai's flat 45, consistent with L2+ already pulling fuel-packaging factors from the same Nicolai Ch. 8 section.
avionics._cite_weight_fraction: Same selection/citation as f16a_L1.json .subsystems.avionics.weight_fraction -- [Raymer Table 11.6, p.375] Fighters 0.03-0.08. DECIDED (Casey, 2026-08-03): midpoint, 0.055.

landing_gear._note: F16LandingGearL2 -- F-16-only, no abstract Base tier (docs/subplans/09_subsystems.md Files to Create). Consumes W_TO (already a plain STATE property on F16WeightsL2) to get the per-wheel load W_w for Raymer's statistical tire-sizing formula.
landing_gear._cite_gear_load_split: [Raymer 6th ed. Ch. 11, p.344, prose]: 'the main tires carry about 90% of the total aircraft weight ... Nose tires carry only about 10% of the static load.' DECIDED default (Casey, 2026-07-31; docs/subplans/09_subsystems.md Equations & Citations §8). The Brandt-workbook-derived alternate split (26.7% main / 73.3% nose, computed by BrandtBalanceStabControl.m off the uncross-checked f16a_geometry.json gear block) is deliberately NOT wired in -- standing, non-blocking discrepancy logged at VnV/BrandtF16A/todo.md, 2026-07-31 entry 'Subsystems deep-dive, Phase A ... gear block provenance and implied gear-load-split'. Comparison data: VnV/BrandtF16A/GroundTruth/f16a_subsystems_ground_truth.json.

tire_sizing._cite_tire_sizing: [Raymer 6th ed., Ch. 11, Table 11.1 'Statistical Tire Sizing,' p.344] Jet fighter/trainer row: D_main[in] = diameter_coeff_A * W_w^diameter_coeff_B, Width_main[in] = width_coeff_A * W_w^width_coeff_B, W_w = static load on one main wheel [lb] (docs/subplans/09_subsystems.md Equations & Citations §9/§9b). The table's other three rows (General aviation A=1.51/B=0.349, Business twin A=2.69/B=0.251, Transport/bomber A=1.63/B=0.315, plus their width coefficients) belong in the future F16LandingGearL2 toolbox code as the full Table 11.1 Constant (same JSON/code split as AeroL1.CLmax_table); this key only records the F-16's own applicable row.

landing_gear._cite_nose_tire_fraction_of_main: [Raymer 6th ed., Ch. 11, Table 11.1 page, prose]: nose tire assumed 60-100% of main-tire size, no F-16-specific point value given (docs/subplans/09_subsystems.md Equations & Citations §9c). DECIDED (Casey, 2026-08-03): use the range midpoint, 0.80 -- the subplan itself calls this 'a designer's choice within a stated range, not a citable point value.' Comparison-report data point: VnV/BrandtF16A/GroundTruth/f16a_subsystems_ground_truth.json's landing_gear_tire_diameter block gives d_nose_ft=1.5 / d_main_ft=2.0, i.e. ratio 0.75 -- close to, but not verification of, this 0.80 pick (that block carries two open provenance/load-split caveats of its own).

Only GRAVIMETRIC specific energy is cited: [Nicolai & Carichner, Table 14.2, p.363] batteries 0.27 kWh/lb (Li-S projected 0.336 kWh/lb by 2015); temp_AI's fast_data.md Table 11 (Mokotoff et al.) gives a generic 0.35-1.55 kWh/kg design-space bound, also gravimetric. Ships as a documented-gap marker, matching TestWeightsL1.testTODO_RaymerTable61CoefficientsNotInRepo's convention (the CLAUDE.md-permitted citation-gap exception) -- NOT a blocker to implementing the liquid-fuel volume path. docs/subplans/09_subsystems.md Equations & Citations §7. RE-CONFIRMED (Casey, 2026-08-03) still open after re-scanning all 31 temp_AI reference-extract files -- including the Nicolai Ch. 12/18-24 extracts newly completed just before this check -- specifically for volumetric-density material; nothing beyond the same Table 14.2 gravimetric figure was found. Remove this key (and add a cited 'battery' sub-block) only when a genuine volumetric energy/pack density is supplied.
subsystems._TODO_gear_bay_volume_packaging: GAP -- no textbook bay-volume (tire+strut stowage) packaging formula was found anywhere in this repo. Raymer's landing-gear chapter (Ch. 11) covers tire/strut/shock-absorber SIZE, not a bay-VOLUME packaging estimate the way Nicolai's Ch. 8 fuel/avionics sections give one; a geometric-envelope assumption (e.g. tire footprint x a retraction-clearance multiplier) would need either a citation or an explicit 'engineering judgment, uncited' label, neither of which is settled. docs/subplans/09_subsystems.md Equations & Citations §11. This means the landing-gear contribution to the Subsystems internal-volume total (Objectives §3) is not yet computable -- tire/strut SIZE (see .landing_gear.tire_sizing above) is unaffected. Remove this key (and add the packaging-formula inputs it would need) only when a source, or an explicitly-labeled uncited assumption, is supplied.

stability_control._note: NOT YET IMPLEMENTED -- no F16SandCL2 class exists yet (docs/subplans/10_stability_control.md, Casey-approved 2026-08-03; io pass 2026-08-03). Longitudinal static stability ONLY, steady level flight -- NO L1 TIER: per docs/subplans/10_stability_control.md's 'Per-equation fidelity resolution' table, all nine of Casey's Raymer 6th ed. Ch. 16 equations resolved to L2/L3 (none to L1), so no f16a_L1.json .stability_control block was created this pass. Universal Ch. 16/16.16-16.18 equation coefficients (Delta x_ac(M) piecewise terms 0.26/0.4/2.5/0.112/0.004; elevator-deflection polynomial 1.576/-3.458/2.882) are NOT duplicated here -- they belong in the future SandCL2/L3 toolbox code as Constants, matching the existing code/JSON split used by AeroL1.CLmax_table and SubsystemsL1's packaging-factor table. Full citation detail: docs/subplans/10_stability_control.md 'Equations & Citations'.
stability_control._geometry_x_station_gap: DECIDED (Casey, 2026-08-03): F16SandCL2 is limited to the CG (x_cg) term ONLY -- see docs/subplans/10_stability_control.md's 'DECIDED: F16SandCL2 is limited to the CG term only' note for the full rationale. F16GeomL2 exposes NO x-station properties at all (confirmed by reading examples/F16A/F16GeomL2.m directly -- only F16GeomL3 has x_apex_wing/x_le_ht/x_le_vt/x_inlet/L_t), so Eqs. 16.4/16.5/16.7/16.8/16.9/16.11/16.12 and 16.13/16.14/16.15 are NOT implemented at L2 at all -- they are L3-ONLY. F16SandCL2 computes only x_cg = Sum(W_i*x_i)/Sum(W_i) over component_x_stations below (using each group's cg_x_ft), with W_i read live by DI from F16WeightsL2 -- no geometry x-stations needed for that term.

component_x_stations._note: DECIDED (Casey, 2026-08-03): built from THIS framework's own WeightsL2/WeightsL3 groups, not the legacy temp_Casey component list -- supersedes this key's earlier 22-row 'component_x_locations' draft (io pass, 2026-08-03), which sourced the legacy sheet directly. Grouped to match F16WeightsL2's own 7 Dependent weight groups (W_wings, W_tail.HT, W_tail.VT, W_fuselage, W_landing_gear, W_installed_engine, W_all_else_empty, W_strake) plus the top-level weights.W_payload_fixed/W_payload_expendable and mission-output W_energy (fuel) -- 10 groups total, WEIGHTS read live by DI from F16WeightsL2, never duplicated here.
component_x_stations._two_station_types_per_group: Casey's instruction (2026-08-03): track BOTH a front_edge_x_ft (the group's geometric leading-edge/apex station, citable to Geometry where it exists) AND a cg_x_ft (an estimated weight-centroid station, since a component's MASS does not sit at its front edge) for every group, as redundant/cross-checkable data, not a single blended number. front_edge_x_ft is NOT itself the CG -- it is kept only as an independent, geometry-citable reference point a future check can compare cg_x_ft against (e.g. cg_x_ft should always be aft of front_edge_x_ft for a part with positive length).
component_x_stations._L2_has_no_front_edge_data: F16GeomL2 exposes NO x-station properties at all (see the block-level _geometry_x_station_gap note above) -- every front_edge_x_ft below is 'N/A (no L2 geometry x-station)' at this fidelity level. This does not block F16SandCL2's CG-only computation (per the DECIDED note above, F16SandCL2 never reads front_edge_x_ft), it only means the redundant cross-check field is unavailable at L2 -- see f16a_L3.json for the same table WITH real front_edge_x_ft values, since F16GeomL3 has the needed properties.
component_x_stations._cg_x_ft_estimate_method: cg_x_ft is an ENGINEERING ESTIMATE, not an independent citation -- computed by mapping the legacy temp_Casey 'Stability&Control' sheet's 22 fine-grained components (docs/subplans/10_stability_control.md 'Ground Truth', live-workbook read, 2026-08-03) into these 10 coarser weight groups and taking each group's OWN weighted-average x-station (Sum(w_i*x_i)/Sum(w_i) over the legacy rows folded into that group) -- i.e. real, live-read component data, re-aggregated to this framework's own grouping, not re-derived from Geometry offsets (which would need an equally uncited LE-to-centroid offset fraction per group anyway -- see the coordinator's prior turn explaining why a purely-Geometry-derived cg_x_ft isn't actually more 'citable' than this). Cross-check: summing all 10 groups' weights below gives 31,368 lbf, within 9 lbf (0.03%) of Brandt's own W_TO=31,377 lbf -- a strong sign the underlying legacy data is a complete, physically real breakdown, even though the GROUPING here is this framework's own, not the legacy sheet's.

stability_control._reuse_c_elev_frac: c_e/c (elevator chord ratio, for the Eq. 16.16/16.18 elevator-deflection sub-formula) is NOT a new S&C input -- F16GeomL2.c_elev_frac already exists (added earlier this session during the tail-sizing/control-surface-sizing absorption into Geometry) and equals 0 (F-16 all-moving stabilator, no separate elevator; Raymer 6th ed. Table 6.5, Fighter/attack row footnote 'Supersonic usually all-moving tail without separate elevator'). The future F16SandCL2 should read obj.geom.c_elev_frac by DI, not duplicate this key. NOTE for the implementation phase: c_elev_frac=0 makes the Eq. 16.16/16.18 elevator-deflection sub-formula for Delta alpha_L0 evaluate to 0 identically for the F-16 -- worth flagging in case that changes how much of Eq. 16.15's scope is actually exercised for this airframe.
stability_control._TODO_x_p: GAP -- x_p (thrust x-location, needed for the F_p*(x_cg-x_p) terms in Eqs. 16.4/16.5/16.7/16.9) is not exposed as a clean input anywhere in this repo. Checked examples/F16A/F16PropL2.m directly: it exposes engine_type, T_SL, T_SL_mil, T_t4_max_F, TSFC_install_factor, bypass_ratio, TR -- no x-location property at all. F16GeomL3 (NOT F16GeomL2, which has no x-stations at all -- see _geometry_x_station_gap above) has x_inlet, L_duct, L_engine, and the Dependent x_nacelle_aft (= x_inlet + L_duct + L_engine, the nozzle-exit station) which COULD serve as a DI-reused proxy for x_p if the implementation phase chooses to source it from Geometry rather than Propulsion -- but that is an implementation-level decision, not io's to make. Legacy SandCLevel3.m hardcodes Xbar_p=33.775 'temporarily' (a documented bug in docs/subplans/10_stability_control.md's Legacy Bugs table) -- do not port that literal. No new JSON key added; flagged as an open input gap, most acute at L2 (zero x-stations available at all here).
stability_control._TODO_i_w_i_h: GAP -- i_w/i_h (wing/horizontal-tail incidence angles, for Eqs. 16.13/16.14) are not exposed anywhere in Geometry. Checked examples/F16A/F16GeomL2.m and F16GeomL3.m directly (grepped for 'incidence'/'i_w'/'i_h'): no such property exists at either level. docs/subplans/10_stability_control.md itself flags this as ambiguous ('if treated as a geometry input rather than an S&C-local constant') and does not resolve it. No citable F-16 incidence value was found in any Scribe-approved source this pass -- NOT invented here. Needs a decision: add i_w/i_h as new Geometry inputs (its own scribe/io pass) or as new S&C-local inputs here, once a cited value is available.
stability_control._no_JSON_for_thrust_correction_terms: Per explicit launch instruction: F_p_alpha, Delta alpha_h/Delta alpha, and Delta alpha_p/Delta alpha (the legacy neutral-point thrust-correction terms) have NO JSON keys anywhere in this file, and none should be added -- docs/subplans/10_stability_control.md's own web cross-check found NO thrust term in the confirmed Eq. 16.9 formula, and Casey's separate note about a '2% reduction per unit prop-to-CG distance, normalized by MAC' correction is unresolved implementation-level territory, not an io decision.
